title: Do two mirror-symmetric superlinear catalysts give self-made cells discrete kinds that breed true, switch rarely through the chemistry's own noise, and respond to a mid-run selection reversal?
summary: Matsubara, Ameta, Thutupalli, Nghe & Krishna (arXiv:2211.03155) show that multistable compartmentalized autocatalytic networks keep heritable compositional states across growth-division regimes and support selection. Per the heredity sweep's reading of the PDF, bistability under growth and dilution needs a reproduction rate that rises with concentration. The collective already sees winner-take-all K_i^2 kinds (c02's two-catalyst micelles) and cross-inhibiting kinds (lab 1's ad2), but those kinds were assigned at seeding or by imposed flips, and c13 named Matsubara only as a pointer. The new parts are variation from the chemistry's own noise, an exactly fitness-matched mirror arm (K1 <-> K2), a parent-daughter composition map (Doulcier et al. 2020) and a mid-run selection reversal.

sources.cite: Matsubara, Ameta, Thutupalli, Nghe & Krishna, Conditions for Darwinian evolution in compartmentalized autocatalytic reaction networks, arXiv:2211.03155 (v2, Jul 2026). Abstract re-opened by the synthesizer; the heredity sweep read the PDF (the r(x) condition, the Fig. 6 reversal).
